title: Jesus Christ Pose - Wikipedia
notes: Badmotorfinger's first single (1991); music by Cornell, Cameron, Shepherd and Thayil. Cameron: 'As soon as I played this pattern everyone dove right in, and within an hour we had the guts of the song.' Thayil: 'Matt's drum part is insane – it's so fast and coordinated.' In 4/4 at 134, D minor, drop D.

title: Outshined - Wikipedia
notes: Badmotorfinger's second single (1991), written by Cornell. 'The verses are in 7/4 time, an unorthodox meter which the band would also later use in Spoonman.' Thayil: odd meters were 'a total accident'.

title: Rusty Cage - Wikipedia
notes: Badmotorfinger's third single (1992), written by Cornell. 'A striking tempo change towards the end': the first part in 4/4, the slower second part 'an irregular, recurring metric pattern containing nineteen beats' (3+3+3+3+2+3+2, or 3+3+3+5+5, or 19/4). Personnel: Matt Cameron, drums.

title: Spoonman - Wikipedia
notes: Superunknown's lead single, 7 February 1994, written by Cornell. 'The main riff was written in septuple meter, in 7/4.' Artis the Spoonman plays spoons; 'Drummer Matt Cameron also plays pots and pans on the song.' Grammy for Best Metal Performance.

title: Black Hole Sun - Wikipedia
notes: Superunknown's third single, 23 May 1994, written by Cornell; the band's signature song. Cameron called it 'a huge departure'. Jon Pareles (New York Times): 'lumpy Ringo Starr-style drumming'. Personnel: Matt Cameron, drums.

title: The Day I Tried to Live - Wikipedia
notes: Superunknown's second single, April 1994, written by Cornell. 'For much of the song, there is a cycle of one measure of 7/4, then two of 4/4.'

title: Fell on Black Days - Wikipedia
notes: Superunknown's last single, 15 November 1994, written by Cornell; in 6/4. Cornell: 'the drums are totally straight, even though the riff is in six, so it doesn't feel quirky at all.'
